genus: Turns a picture into a 3D model
free_tier: 1 try a day without an account; downloading the 3D file needs more
licence_note: MIT licence for the model and code; some rendering dependencies have their own licences.
launched_note: Weights published 1 Dec 2025; Space 10 Dec 2025; paper 16 Dec 2025.
plan: Free, logged out (no account, no token)
test: One creature concept drawing (licensed, background keyed out) to 3D on the official Space, Space defaults, one attempt; then Extract GLB.

conditions.value: 1 cartoon dragon drawing (free from Unsplash), with its background cut out
The demo's own background remover was refusing visitors without an account; the demo asks for a cut-out anyway
TRELLIS 2's official free demo page, in a web browser
1, no retries (the demo was busy 23 times before it let us in)
Refused: the preview used up the free daily allowance
Us, running the demo page automatically

runs.result: raw/auto/views/ (6 render modes x 8 angles, the Space's own preview)
runs.observed: One coherent creature: both wings, horns, claws and the tail curve kept. Seen side-on, the tail is a broad flat paddle.

glb_attempt.error: You have exceeded your ZeroGPU quota (120s requested vs. 0s left)

seconds_to_result_note: Wall clock from submitting Generate to the preview arriving (40.7 s), measured by scripts/auto_capture_trellis2.py; the status stream showed no separate queue phase, so queue time is not subtracted.

flaw.detail: Seen side-on, a view the drawing never showed, the tail is a broad flat paddle instead of a round tail.

verdict_reason: One flat cartoon drawing became a full 3D dragon in 41 seconds, free and with no account, with the wings, horns and claws kept. Seen from the side, the tail is flat like a paddle, and without an account you can look at the model but not download it.

free_tier_parts.completeness: GLB export locked behind more quota 6

lesson: Give it a clean cut-out of your drawing, and expect to fix the sides the drawing never showed.
